In this video, we explain how most people misunderstand writing because they treat it as self-expression, when it is really applied psychology. We break this down through the Soham Parekh cold email example, showing how great writing works like a psychological program. We then get into the core lesson here: world-building. How the goal is not what we want to say, but what the reader actually reads.

We then connect this directly to AI and prompting. How a vague prompt produces generic output because the model fills gaps with defaults, while a detailed prompt creates a clear universe with rules the AI can operate inside.

The takeaway is that writing well and prompting well are the same underlying skill, and why controlled framing is one of the highest-leverage form of communication.
